transcript:
Meeting header: Horizon Silo x Redwood discovery
Date: 2026-03-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Oliver Park (Horizon Silo - Head of Platform), Naomi Ishikawa (Lead SRE), Devon Marks (CTO), Sanae Ito (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Horizon Silo is exploring a hybrid onramp for GPU inference; primary drivers are cost predictability, data residency, and burst capacity.
- They want a pilot that runs internal benchmarks and validates VPC/private deployment.
- Next steps: security docs, network diagram, benchmark run, pricing.

Topics: requirements, networking/VPC, dedicated vs hosted, pilot scope, timelines, procurement

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um i'll kick off, i'm maya from redwood, uh we're the ae on this, with me is ethan our solutions eng and priya who'll help on success.
00:14 Oliver Park: hi thanks, i'm oliver, i'm running platform at horizon silo, happy to be here. quick note, we're on a somewhat tight timeline for a q3 launch.
00:25 Ethan Reyes: great, so maybe quick agenda: gather constraints (network, compliance), talk workload shapes (seq len, qps), then pilot framing. sound ok?
00:34 Naomi Ishikawa: yes that's perfect. and hi, naomi here, lead sre, i'm mainly curious about VPC connectivity and key management.
00:42 Devon Marks: devon here, cto, i'll be listening on architecture and procurement lane. i may drop off at 37 because of another call.
00:51 Maya Chen: awesome. can you tell us current infra? like are you running inference in-house today?
01:02 Oliver Park: we have a mix — a couple on-prem ai boxes and some cloud capacity on CloudForge for bursts. mostly for embeddings and rerank right now, but moving to a gen-lm feature.
01:18 Ethan Reyes: ok, can you share typical request profile? tokens per request, concurrency, cold starts?
01:27 Naomi Ishikawa: typical seq lengths are 256-1024 tokens, bursts up to 120 concurrent reqs for peak, sustained around 20-30. latency target sub-200ms for critical routes.
01:45 Maya Chen: good. and data residency — any restrictions?
01:48 Oliver Park: yes, all PII must stay in their VPC, so a private deployment or VPC peering is essential. can't ship PII to third-party managed spaces without controls.
02:05 Ethan Reyes: understood. Redwood has private deployment modes — our private control plane with a customer-managed VPC option, and dedicated reserved capacity if you want predictable throughput.
02:16 Devon Marks: how much ops overhead is private vs dedicated hosted? we don't want to rebuild infra patterns.
02:23 Ethan Reyes: private requires some initial network setup (peering, firewall rules, KMS setup), but we provide automation scripts. Dedicated is hosted but reserved GPU pools — less network work but needs data controls. tradeoff is control vs ops.
02:40 Maya Chen: quick question: do you have an HSM/KMS provider?
02:44 Naomi Ishikawa: we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed key.
02:50 Ethan Reyes: great that's straightforward for Redwood Private; we integrate with AWS KMS, HSMs via standard key wraps — small config.
03:00 Oliver Park: ok on capacity — what's the cost delta between dedicated and hosted? rough numbers fine.
03:08 Maya Chen: i'll send indicative pricing in the follow-up — but as rule of thumb, dedicated reserved capacity gives better per-token economics for sustained workloads; hosted is better for variable low volume. we'll include example math for your QPS.
03:21 Devon Marks: for our pilot, we want to validate latency at 200ms p95 and 1k token bursts. can you support perf testing?
03:30 Ethan Reyes: yes, we can run a benchmark with your sample model or a comparable open model. we'll provide a script that exercises batching, kv cache behavior, and warm/cold starts.
03:40 Naomi Ishikawa: curious about KV cache — we've seen docs where cache improves perf for chat but complicates multi-tenant isolation; any pitfalls?
03:51 Ethan Reyes: good point. Redwood's KV cache can be per-tenant on private/dedicated, and we have controls for eviction and sharding. sometimes it's mis-labeled in older docs as KV cash, haha. but technically safe.
04:05 Sanae Ito: from procurement, what's the shortest contract for a pilot? we prefer a time-boxed engagement, not multi-year commitments.
04:13 Maya Chen: pilots can be month-to-three-months, with pilot credits and a short MSA addendum if needed. procurement will get a sample PO template.
04:24 Oliver Park: does redwood provide audit logs? we need to show access logs and invocation logs for auditors.
04:30 Priya Nair: we do — per-request logs, token-level cost breakdowns, model versioning, and audit trails. retention windows configurable.
04:40 Naomi Ishikawa: what about throughput scaling? bursts up to 120 concurrent, but we also want headroom for a spike to 250 for a short period.
04:50 Ethan Reyes: autoscaling policies can handle burst capacity if you use Dedicated with burst pool, or Private with autoscale hooks. you can set a policy to keep X reserved and allow Y burst. we can show historical examples.
05:05 Devon Marks: what about quantization? will we lose output fidelity if we move to int8 or 4-bit?
05:12 Ethan Reyes: depends on the model — Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per model and workload; we can run evals on your prompt set to measure delta and recommend quant profiles that preserve quality.
05:26 Oliver Park: security — need SOC2 and ISO docs. also SSO/SAML, RBAC.
05:33 Maya Chen: we'll attach SOC2, ISO pieces along with SAML/SSO integration guides. RBAC is available in console.
05:40 Naomi Ishikawa: any experience with air-gapped on-prem installs? we might have a later stage project where that's required.
05:47 Ethan Reyes: yes, we have an on-prem package; it requires offline install steps and an airgap checklist. it's more labor but supported. we can start with VPC private deployment and revisit air-gap later.
06:00 Oliver Park: assumptions for the pilot: we want to run a 2-week perf suite against 2 model sizes, then a short integration test in our staging VPC. is that feasible?
06:12 Ethan Reyes: totally. typical pilot flow: 1) network + auth setup, 2) benchmark run with sample model, 3) integration test, 4) results + ops handoff. should fit in 3-4 weeks if we align schedules.
06:26 Maya Chen: ok timeline — you mentioned q3 launch; procurement often is the gating factor. sanae, do you have an internal procurement target?
06:33 Sanae Ito: aiming to finalize vendor shortlist by mid-april, contract signed by end of may. pilot in april would be ideal.
06:40 Maya Chen: noted. we'll aim to have pilot artifacts by late march so you can run pilot in april.
06:48 Oliver Park: network specifics: we prefer VPC peering to avoid egress, and allowed CIDR blocks is important. we'll share the list.
06:57 Ethan Reyes: we'll send a network diagram and a redwood onramp checklist with required rules and ports.
07:04 Naomi Ishikawa: monitoring — we need traces tied back to request ids, and token-level breakdowns to map cost to teams.
07:12 Priya Nair: that's in the console — per-route dashboards, token cost, and tracing hooks to integrate with your APM.
07:20 Devon Marks: any customers with similar stack (hybrid on-prem + cloud)? references would help.
07:28 Maya Chen: yes, we can share a reference list; i'll include 2-3 customers in the follow-up who did hybrid onramp pilots, obfuscated for NDA.
07:36 Oliver Park: competitors — we've looked at CloudForge, MatrixAI, NimbusCon; what's Redwood's edge?
07:44 Maya Chen: we focus on consistent runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, plus tooling for cost controls (batching, cache, quantization recommendations) and strong rollouts. not just endpoints, but operational predictability.
07:59 Naomi Ishikawa: ok specifics on firewall and ports?
08:04 Ethan Reyes: standard TLS endpoints, peering with private subnet, and a few control ports for health checks. we'll include exact port list in the network doc.
08:14 Sanae Ito: legal — any special data processing addendum?
08:19 Maya Chen: we have a DPA and can add clauses for data residency; i'll loop legal after this call.
08:28 Oliver Park: for the benchmark, which metrics will you capture? p95 latency, p50, cpu/gpu utilization, token cost, and maybe tail lat?
08:38 Ethan Reyes: yes, plus KV hit rate, batch sizes, memory pressure, and GPU power states if you want.
08:45 Devon Marks: do you need sample model weights or can you run open-model equivalents?
08:50 Ethan Reyes: both options. if you can share representative model artifacts we can run exact parity tests; otherwise we'll pick open models with similar architecture and seq lengths.
08:59 Naomi Ishikawa: question about failover — if a dedicated pool is saturated, does Redwood auto-fall back to hosted?
09:06 Ethan Reyes: there are routing policies — you can set fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or to hosted, with configurable fallback thresholds.
09:16 Maya Chen: ok quick mid-call recap: send network + KMS details, we'll send SOC2 and sample contract, ethan will prep benchmark script, and we'll schedule pilot week of 29th. sound right?
09:29 Oliver Park: yes, that matches.
09:32 Sanae Ito: budget questions — will you provide pilot credits?
09:36 Maya Chen: yes we typically provide pilot credits; i'll include proposed amount and how it's applied in the follow-up.
09:44 Devon Marks: any gotchas for model quantization across GPUs? e.g., mixed precision differences across vendor kernels?
09:52 Ethan Reyes: kernels vary; our compilation layer picks the best kernel per backend. we'll call out vendor-specific notes in the benchmark report. sometimes small differences in generation probabilities appear, so evals matter.
10:05 Naomi Ishikawa: timeline again: when can we expect network doc and security pack?
10:10 Maya Chen: i'll send both by 2026-03-23.
10:14 Oliver Park: and the benchmark script?
10:17 Ethan Reyes: aiming for 2026-03-28 with runbook.
10:22 Maya Chen: great. any other concerns from your side?
10:26 Naomi Ishikawa: licensing of open models — we may need clarity on redistribution if we host model artifacts.
10:31 Ethan Reyes: we'll include license guidance; for private deployments you can bring your own model and control licensing.
10:38 Devon Marks: procurement will need an SOW for the pilot.
10:41 Maya Chen: we'll provide a simple SOW and MSA addendum template.
10:46 Oliver Park: ok last technical nit — how does Redwood handle cold starts for very long sequences? we've seen spikes in tail lat.
10:54 Ethan Reyes: we use continuous batching and prefix cache to mitigate; for very long sequences we recommend chunking and tuned batch settings. the benchmark will help pick parameters.
11:10 Maya Chen: closing time — quick recap and owners:
11:14 Maya Chen: maya will send network diagram, SOC2 pack, pilot pricing (owner: maya, due 2026-03-25)
11:20 Ethan Reyes: ethan will prepare bench script, runbook, and config examples (owner: ethan, due 2026-03-28)
11:26 Devon Marks: devon to share model samples and QPS profile (owner: devon, due 2026-03-24)
11:32 Sanae Ito: sanae to share procurement timeline and PO template (owner: sanae, due 2026-03-30)
11:38 Oliver Park: thanks team, we'll ingest docs and aim to pick a pilot window in april.
11:44 Priya Nair: we'll set a follow-up for a pilot kickoff once docs are in — i'll send calendar options.
11:50 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up by eod tomorrow with the network checklist and security pack.
11:58 Devon Marks: thanks, bye.
12:00 End of recording
